background.executionContext:
**Commands used:**
1. `./b4w.ps1 help` — Read CLI help (discovery)
2. `./b4w.ps1 goto "https://www.amazon.com"` — Navigate to Amazon
3. `./b4w.ps1 snapshot -v 0 --stdout` — **FAILED** (PowerShell flag interception)
4. `./b4w.ps1 -- snapshot -v 0 --stdout` — **FAILED** (PowerShell parameter ambiguity)
5. `./b4w.sh snapshot -v 0 --stdout` — Success (used b4w.sh workaround)
6. `./b4w.sh fill e37666 "Laser-Engraved Crystal"` — Fill search
7. `./b4w.sh press Enter` — Submit search → search results page
8. `./b4w.sh htmlsnapshot` — Capture HTML snapshot
9. `./b4w.sh htmlsnapshot inspect` — Auto-discover patterns (limited results)
10. `./b4w.sh reload` — **FAILED** (navigated to about:blank)
11. `./b4w.sh goto "https://www.amazon.com/s?k=Laser-Engraved+Crystal"` — **FAILED** (Amazon 503/anti-bot)
12. Recovered via Amazon homepage search form
13. `./b4w.sh htmlsnapshot capture` — **FAILED** ("Nil url is not allowed")
14. Multiple iterations to get working htmlsnapshot + data extraction
15. `./b4w.sh htmlsnapshot query --sql @query.sql` — X-SQL extraction (partial success)
16. `./b4w.sh htmlsnapshot get all text` + `get all attr` — Extracted titles, URLs, prices
17. `./b4w.sh goto "https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0FCLQZDHV"` — DNA Crystal detail page
18. `./b4w.sh goto "https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0DPHQ818J"` — Solar System detail page
19. `./b4w.sh goto "https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0D9KLS8KK"` — Wolf Crystal detail page

**Important decisions:**
- Switched from `b4w.ps1` to `b4w.sh` after flag interception issues
- Abandoned `eval` approach after it returned empty results
- Used `htmlsnapshot get all` (individual queries) instead of X-SQL for correlated data extraction
- Visited only 3 of 10 detail pages due to time constraints, relying on search-result data for the remaining 7

**Workarounds required:**
- `b4w.sh` instead of `b4w.ps1` for commands with short flags
- Re-searching from homepage instead of direct URL navigation (anti-bot)
- Multiple re-attempts of `htmlsnapshot` capture after "Nil url" errors

issues.title: htmlsnapshot capture fails with 'Nil url is not allowed' after session state loss

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: 1. Navigate to a URL, 2. Run reload (triggers about:blank bug), 3. Navigate to a new URL, 4. Run htmlsnapshot capture

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: HTML snapshot is captured for the current page.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: ERROR: html_snapshot_capture failed: Nil url is not allowed

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: After the about:blank bug invalidates the session state, the backend's URL tracking for the session appears to become corrupted or null. Subsequent navigation doesn't properly restore the URL tracking, so htmlsnapshot_capture fails because it can't determine the page URL. This is a cascading failure from the reload bug.

sections.label: Code Pointer
sections.body: MCPToolController.kt or the htmlsnapshot capture handler — the URL resolution logic should fall back to reading the current page URL from the browser if the tracked URL is nil

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Fix the root cause (reload → about:blank bug)
- Add defensive fallback: if tracked URL is nil, read current URL from browser via CDP Runtime.evaluate('window.location.href')
- Add a clear error message suggesting the user run 'goto' again to re-establish session state

issues.title: eval returns empty string for document.title even after network idle

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: Navigate to any page, wait --load networkidle, then eval 'document.title' --json

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: The page title as a JSON string.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: {"command":"eval","output":{"expression":"document.title","result":""},"status":"ok"}

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: The eval command may be executing JavaScript in the wrong execution context (e.g., an empty iframe, extension context, or a frame that hasn't loaded). The status is 'ok' but the result is empty, suggesting the JS ran but against the wrong target.

sections.label: Code Pointer
sections.body: Likely in PulsarWebDriver.kt or the eval tool executor — the Runtime.evaluate call may not be targeting the main frame

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Ensure eval targets the main/top-level frame, not a child iframe
- Add --frame or --context option for explicit frame targeting
- The empty result should produce a warning, not silently return ''
- Add integration tests: eval 'document.title' should return the page title shown in goto output

sections.body: The auto-discovery analyzes the first child of :root which happens to be a navigation element on the Amazon page. The algorithm favors elements with high repetition at the top of the DOM, which on many modern e-commerce sites are navigation menus, not product grids.

sections.label: Code Pointer
sections.body: The htmlsnapshot inspect algorithm — needs to prioritize main content area elements or try multiple root-level candidates

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Skip navigation elements (nav, header, footer) in the auto-discovery
- Start analysis from main content area (main, #main, [role=main]) if available
- Add a --deep flag that searches for repeating patterns at any depth
- Integrate with PowerCSS :expr() to find visually similar card-like elements (similar width/height)

issues.title: X-SQL DOM_FIRST_TEXT fails to extract product titles from Amazon search results

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: Run X-SQL: SELECT DOM_FIRST_TEXT(DOM, 'h2 a span') AS title FROM DOM_LOAD_AND_SELECT(@url, '[data-component-type="s-search-result"]')

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: Product titles extracted from h2 a span elements inside each search result card.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: Title field is empty string for all results. Prices and ratings are correctly extracted.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: Amazon's h2 elements inside search result cards may not contain a span child matching 'h2 a span'. The actual DOM structure may use different nesting (e.g., h2 > a > span or h2 > a with text directly). The selector 'h2 a span' doesn't match Amazon's actual markup.

sections.label: Code Pointer
sections.body: The X-SQL DOM_FIRST_TEXT function or the CSS selector needs adjustment. Amazon product titles use a.a-link-normal.s-line-clamp-4 rather than h2 a span.

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Add a Debug mode for X-SQL that shows which elements matched each DOM_ function
- Improve the htmlsnapshot inspect output to suggest selectors for product titles specifically
- Document common Amazon/e-commerce selectors in the htmlsnapshot-scenarios.md reference

issues.title: No auto-HTML-snapshot after goto — extra step required before extraction

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: Run goto to navigate, then immediately run htmlsnapshot get text 'h1'

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: The HTML snapshot is implicitly captured or the get command works against the live page.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: ERROR: 'Nil url is not allowed'. User must explicitly run htmlsnapshot capture first.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: goto auto-captures an AX-tree snapshot (for click/fill refs) but does not auto-capture an HTML snapshot (for css selector extraction). Users must always run htmlsnapshot as a separate explicit step.

sections.label: Code Pointer
sections.body: MCPToolController.kt goto handler — consider auto-capturing an HTML snapshot alongside the AX-tree snapshot

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Auto-capture HTML snapshot on goto (like AX snapshot is auto-captured)
- Or make htmlsnapshot get fall back to capturing if no snapshot exists
- Document this requirement more prominently in the Quick Patterns section
- The 'Nil url is not allowed' error message should include a hint: 'Did you forget to run htmlsnapshot first?'

issues.title: Amazon anti-bot detection causes silent failure when navigating to search URLs directly

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: Navigate directly to https://www.amazon.com/s?k=Laser-Engraved+Crystal in a fresh or stale session.

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: Search results page loads normally.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: Amazon shows 'Sorry! Something went wrong!' (503-type error page). The CLI reports success with the error page URL.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: Amazon's anti-bot detection flags direct navigation to search URLs without a proper session/cookie context. The homepage → search form flow establishes a valid session that direct URL navigation doesn't.

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Add a status code check after goto and warn if the page is an error page (status != 200 or title contains 'Sorry')
- Consider adding a cookie/header preset for common e-commerce sites
- Document the homepage-search-form flow as the recommended approach for Amazon in the scenario docs

issues.title: Ref lifecycle and snapshot frequency create cognitive load for simple data extraction tasks

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: As a new user, attempt to extract product data from search results: navigate → snapshot → extract.

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: Straightforward: navigate to the page, extract data.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: User must understand: (1) AX snapshot vs HTML snapshot distinction, (2) refs are ephemeral, (3) htmlsnapshot must be explicitly captured before get/query, (4) viewport pagination for large pages, (5) interactive mode strips generic divs (bad for e-commerce). This is a lot of conceptual overhead for a simple extraction task.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: The design separates page interaction (snapshot/refs) from data extraction (htmlsnapshot/css selectors) into two distinct workflows with different state management. While this separation is architecturally sound, it's not obvious to new users.

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Implement a unified 'scrape' command that handles htmlsnapshot capture + extraction in one step
- Add a 'quick-extract' workflow that auto-discovers selectors on Amazon/e-commerce pages
- In the Core Loop (SKILL.md line 17-24), add a parallel 'Extraction Loop' showing the htmlsnapshot workflow
- The tip after 'goto' could mention: 'For data extraction, run htmlsnapshot next'
